clue.text: Marine being Nero was one to see emperor's end in hired vehicle

parts.note: Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned, so he was a fiddler

indicators.note: the emperor's last letter is placed inside the word for a hired vehicle

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle hired for a journey

indicators.note: the end of the word emperor is its final letter

explanation.surface: A bizarre claim that Nero went to see a fellow emperor's death in a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nero was one' leans on the legend that Nero fiddled while Rome burned; 'Marine being' is the definition, a sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler crab is a sea-shore crustacean, a marine creature, named for the male's one oversized claw.

clue.text: Indeed an evil axis promoting horrible fen across desk?

parts.note: to be for something is to promote or support it

indicators.note: horrible suggests the words are mangled, so the letters of fen, across and desk are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dramatic warning about a malign alliance pushing a dreadful marsh across someone's desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges all three words as one pool, after the piece for 'promoting'. 'Indeed' only links, and the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a sinister alliance of evil powers, as in the battle of good against wickedness.

clue.text: See 1
Primate, leader in life or lives

indicators.note: the leader of the word life is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
lives means exists, as is does

explanation.surface: A motto that a leader matters in life or death, read with a primate in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A loris is a small, slow-moving nocturnal primate of southern Asia.

clue.text: Green screen feature

parts.note: green means raw or inexperienced
to screen something is to hide it

explanation.surface: A green screen, the backdrop film-makers use for special effects.
explanation.walkthrough: Rawhide was a long-running American television western, so 'feature' points to it as a screen production.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen feature is a film or show, and Rawhide was a famous TV western series.

clue.text: See 17
Use of Eden and Blair beyond which one might earn no crust?

definitions.text: beyond which one might earn no crust?

indicators.note: making use of these names suggests their letters are reworked into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about how two British Prime Ministers' policies left people unable to make a living.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Eden and Tony Blair were British Prime Ministers; only their surnames' letters matter. 'crust' plays on bread as money.
explanation.definitionFit: Below the poverty line, the minimum income level, one could not afford even a crust.

clue.text: Pool of despair

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the word despair

explanation.surface: A dramatic phrase about sinking into a pool of despair.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a mineral spring or pool where people bathe.

clue.text: Pig outside had to follow every movement

indicators.note: the pig word goes round the outside of had

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A pig standing outside having to trail someone's every move.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to tail them secretly, tracking each step.

clue.text: Apostle to wander off

indicators.note: off suggests the word wander has gone wrong, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A follower of Jesus inclined to stray from the path.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew, brother of Peter, was one of the twelve disciples of Jesus.

clue.text: More bloody time travels backwards in prestigious vehicle

indicators.note: the reversed time word sits inside the abbreviation for the posh car

parts.note: RR stands for Rolls-Royce, a prestigious car

indicators.note: the word for time is read from end to start

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A time-travel story set in a luxury car that gets increasingly gory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travels backwards' turns the time word round before it goes inside the Rolls-Royce letters; 'bloody' means undercooked, as of steak.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked rare is bloody, so rarer means bloodier, less cooked.

clue.text: Dante's law flouted in Eliot's wilderness

indicators.note: a flouted law is broken, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A literary jibe that T.S. Eliot ignored Dante's rules in his poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: T.S. Eliot's famous poem The Waste Land is the wilderness meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliot's 1922 poem pictures modern life as a barren, desolate landscape.

clue.text: Girl as queen is French embraced by 9

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, queen

indicators.note: the French word is held within the number

parts.note: the number nine written as a word
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A girl described as a queen hugged by a numeral, read as a riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' here is simply the number nine, not a cross-reference to 9-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernestine is a female first name.

clue.text: Outlaw Act!

definitions.meaning: the ... were the outlaw clan in R.D. Blackmore's novel Lorna ...
read as an order to perform one act

explanation.surface: A single command to an outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Carver Doone is the villainous outlaw of Blackmore's novel; split, the letters say perform a single deed.

clue.text: Old and decrepit NHS — Swedish money's put towards the land

indicators.note: something decrepit is broken down, so the letters NHS are rearranged

parts.note: the ore is a Swedish coin, a hundredth of a krona

explanation.surface: A complaint that Swedish cash is being spent shoring up the run-down British health service.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: An onshore wind or current moves from the sea in to the coast.

clue.text: Lynn's in most of war machine, typically

indicators.note: the singer's first name goes inside the shortened siege engine
most of the word means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: an onager was an ancient catapult used in siege warfare
Vera Lynn was the British wartime singer; 's reads as is

explanation.surface: A wartime singer stationed inside a weapon of war, as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Vera Lynn was the 'Forces' Sweetheart' of WWII Britain. 'most of' cuts the last letter from the catapult, and 'in' places the singer inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Typically and on average both mean as a general rule, usually.

clue.text: No allies at sea, but she loved a hero

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of no allies are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lonely woman adrift without friends, yet in love with a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The hero is Superman, whom the reporter loved.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Planet reporter in the comics is Superman's sweetheart.

clue.text: A royal pair caught in blast settle down

indicators.note: the royal letters are held inside the horn blast

parts.note: a toot is a blast on a horn
K for king and ER for queen give a royal couple
K for king and ER for queen give a royal couple

explanation.surface: A king and queen trapped in an explosion trying to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that takes root establishes itself; figuratively, a person becomes settled.

clue.text: Bard returns (with Shakes!) to promote philosopher

indicators.note: shaking the words jumbles their letters

parts.note: to sell an idea is to promote it

explanation.surface: Shakespeare comes back, waving his arms, to promote a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shakes' plays on Shakespeare, the Bard, but is the anagram signal for BARD RETURNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertrand Russell was the British logician and thinker of Principia Mathematica.

clue.text: See 15
Some rest on Ianthe's land

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: Part of the property that Ianthe owns.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country, a land in northern Europe.

clue.text: Talk with rhetoric outlines training run

indicators.note: the speech word goes around the outside of the training letters

parts.note: to orate is to speak grandly
PE is physical education, training

explanation.surface: Grand speech that sketches out a practice course.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a machine or business is to operate it.

clue.text: Cocaine translates into various languages

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective that names a group of languages

indicators.note: translating changes a word's form, so the letters of cocaine are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drug's name rendered into a number of tongues.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oceanic tongues are a large branch of the Austronesian family spoken across the Pacific.

clue.text: Soul mate for Cupid

definitions.meaning: the Greek word for the spirit or mind
in myth the god of love married a mortal princess

explanation.surface: Finding a soulmate for the god of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Psyche is Greek for the spirit, and in myth the princess who became Cupid's wife.

clue.text: Tabloid exposed, stew results

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a cheap newspaper
out means revealed or exposed

explanation.surface: A tabloid exposé leads to trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a highly seasoned meat and vegetable stew.

clue.text: Say bother

definitions.meaning: to be in a bother or fluster

explanation.definitionFit: To state is to declare; a state is also an agitated condition, a fuss.

clue.text: Most with it drowns?

parts.note: read as a picture: one who drowns dies inside a river, here the Trent

explanation.surface: A question whether the most fashionable person drowns.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a major English river; putting DIES inside TRENT gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: With it means fashionable, so the most with it is the most fashionable.

clue.text: Cook had a place turned over

indicators.note: the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to have lived somewhere is to have had a place there

explanation.surface: A cook whose home was flipped upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To devil food is to cook it with hot spices and mustard.

clue.text: Early one to sing about his species without a note

indicators.note: the singing word goes around the rest

parts.note: to croon is to sing softly

indicators.note: without means outside, so the species word surrounds the note

parts.note: man is the human species
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A prehistoric person crooning about mankind but missing a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so MAN goes round G to give MAGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cro-Magnon was an early modern human of the European Stone Age.

clue.text: Impaler all but impaled by priestess, a literary lady-boy

indicators.note: the priestess pierces the shortened impaler, sitting inside it
all but means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Vlad the Impaler was a Wallachian ruler
Io was a priestess of Hera in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A gruesome tale of a tyrant run through by a priestess, with a cross-dressing heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Viola in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night disguises herself as the young man Cesario.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's heroine spends most of Twelfth Night dressed as a youth.

clue.text: English paper appears again in history?

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: An English newspaper reprinting a story from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eft' is an archaic word, so 'in history' signals an old usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Eft once meant afterwards or a second time, surviving in eftsoons.

clue.text: Made less potent ale: Muscadet's volcanic!

indicators.note: something volcanic erupts violently, so these letters are blown apart and rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Wine-tasting notes claiming beer and white wine are explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: Muscadet is a dry white wine from the Loire.
explanation.definitionFit: To emasculate is to weaken or deprive of strength or virility.
